The two gates

Gate 1 — Sign

Signing freezes a cut into a TEP. The gate refuses:

  • an empty cut;

  • a change with no acceptance criteria ("nothing proves this");

  • a change with no grounding (no place in the code);

  • an ask in the cut with an undecided question;

  • documentation missing: the cut lands no page under docs/ and carries no written exemption.

Documentation is required for every cut, always — this holds regardless of thinkubeTandem.docsGateMode, which governs Gate 2 only (below). The one way past it is a written exemption: before signing, say documentation is not needed and type why. A blank reason is refused. The reason is recorded once for the whole cut, stamped on the signed cut alongside the signing moment, and bound by the signature — editing it afterwards shows up as drift, the same as editing any other grounded content.

The click mints TEP-<you>-<n> and a machine-local HMAC token bound to the pair you actually saw: the rendered cut screen plus the grounded content underneath it. There is no expiry — instead, any edit to the signed content makes the token stop matching, and dispatch refuses until you sign again. What runs is exactly what you approved, enforced cryptographically rather than by convention.

Gate 2 — Accept

A delivery page lists every proof: one per acceptance criterion, executed by the real closing gate, plus the repository’s own test suite. Accepting:

  • is refused while any proof is not green;

  • is refused while a declared documentation obligation is unmet (the docs gate blocks by default; thinkubeTandem.docsGateMode: advisory is the recorded escape hatch);

  • runs in the canonical order merge → stamp → retire: a refused merge aborts before anything is stamped; worktree cleanup is best-effort and never fails a landed accept.

Everything that did NOT arrive is printed on the page — UNDELIVERED items, confessions found by the honesty scan, unmet obligations. Red is shown as red; there is no override.
